title: Bitcoin Hovers Near $80,000 as ETF Outflows and $100 Oil Weigh on Crypto
excerpt: Ethereum held near $2,370 as $636 million left US spot Bitcoin ETFs, $467 million in leveraged bets were liquidated, and crude above $100 kept pressure on risk assets.
body:
• Bitcoin hovered near $80,000 on Saturday, trading around $80,650-$80,860, with Ethereum near $2,370-$2,380, as both fell for another session.
  • US spot Bitcoin ETFs swung back to net outflows, with about $636 million in withdrawals erasing the prior sessions' inflows, according to The Block's data.
  • Brent crude above $100 and concerns about AI financing are tightening liquidity and pressuring risk assets, traders said.
  • About $467 million in leveraged positions were liquidated in 24 hours, roughly 69% of them long bets.

Bitcoin traded near $80,000 on Saturday and Ethereum held around $2,370, extending a slide that has pulled the largest cryptocurrency roughly 36% below its all-time high of $126,156, as macro uncertainty and weakening institutional demand weighed on digital assets.

Bitcoin changed hands between $80,650 and $80,860 through the day, down about 1%, while Ethereum traded near $2,374-$2,381, according to market data compiled by The Economic Times and CoinGecko-based trackers. The total crypto market was worth about $2.8 trillion, with Bitcoin's share of the largest tokens rising as altcoins fell harder — XRP lost about 2.2% to $1.29 and Solana slid about 1.6% to near $102.

ETF flows turn against the market

The institutional bid that supported prices earlier this year has faded. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $636 million in net withdrawals in the latest session, wiping out a four-session run of inflows totalling roughly $443 million, according to The Block data summarised by Coinjuice. Trading firm QCP Capital said concerns about AI financing had spread from equities into crypto, adding to selling pressure — the same AI-spending anxiety that has hit technology stocks this month.

Leverage amplified the move. Roughly $467 million in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, affecting about 180,000 traders, with long positions accounting for about 69% of the wipeout, according to market trackers cited by CryptoPotato via CryptoRank, which noted Bitcoin had been rejected at $85,000 on Wednesday before sliding toward $80,000.

Oil is the macro channel

The mechanism linking crude to crypto is rates. Brent has traded above $100 a barrel amid Middle East supply risk, feeding inflation pressure at a moment when investors are already debating how long the Federal Reserve must keep policy restrictive. Higher energy costs raise transport and production prices, which keeps inflation sticky, which in turn limits the Fed's room to cut — a sequence that drains liquidity from speculative assets first. Bitcoin has traded as a high-beta risk asset through this cycle, not as the haven its advocates describe.

What traders are watching

The $80,000 level is the line in focus: analysts cited in market coverage describe an $80,000-$86,000 channel, and a sustained break below $80,000 would open the way to deeper losses after the rejection at $85,000. ETF flow data early next week will show whether the $636 million withdrawal was a one-day exit or the start of a trend. This article is market reporting, not investment advice; crypto positions held by diaspora investors through US ETFs will track the same flows. Sentiment gauges sat in neutral territory on Saturday, a sign the sell-off has been orderly rather than panicked, though thin weekend liquidity can exaggerate moves in either direction.
